execution.nextRequiredOwner: bubbles.design, to resolve the one open Definition of Done row in Scope 1. Thirteen of the fourteen rows are earned. The last asks for a red-green probe proving each new assertion fails when the guard is removed, and TB-020-03 has no single guard. A later round widened the enumeration and corrected its layer count from three to four: E1 the arithmetic origin, E2 the CO-1 assembly, E3 the display seam and R2 the raw-stringification fallback each sit on this assertion's path, and each was removed alone and returned exit 7. E2 and E3 each carry a live-mutation control on the identical literal, TB-020-01 and TB-020-04 respectively, both exit 0, so the exit 7 is assertion blindness rather than an inert mutation. E4 was removed alone as well and is recorded as uninformative, because the acceptance fixture declares no disposition and nothing in the acceptance set exercises it. P6d shows the assertion is over-determined rather than vacuous by neutralising every finiteness guard in rltax.js at once, which does make it fail. Closing the row honestly needs either a harness that composes mutations or a design amendment naming the true adversarial case for an over-determined assertion.
